title: FancyZones Issue with msedge.exe Apps
author: JStockCo
summary: Distinct Edge PWAs share FancyZones last-known-zone placement, matching the established Chromium PWA identity tracker and its open AUMID-qualified implementation attempt.

status.label: Existing PWA placement work
status.detail: Issue 652 owns the behavior, and PR 41656 contains an unmerged implementation attempt.

next_action.label: Post duplicate guidance
next_action.reason: Consolidate the Edge PWA report with the active canonical tracker and implementation attempt.

judgment.rationale: The report is the same FancyZones browser/PWA last-known-zone identity collision tracked by Issue 652. Current code keys history by process path, and the open PR 41656 implements the matching AppUserModelID-qualified approach.
evidence: The reporter describes multiple Edge PWAs hosted by msedge.exe or msedge_proxy.exe sharing last-known-zone placement.
Issue 652 remains open for Chromium Edge PWA last-known-zone support.
Issue 34713 was closed as a duplicate of Issue 652.
Current AppZoneHistory history lookup is process-path based.
PR 41656 appends PKEY_AppUserModel_ID to the process identity used for zone history, but remains open and unmerged.
judgment.recommended_action: Close as a duplicate of Issue 652 while directing validation and implementation discussion to that tracker and PR 41656.

fix_assessment.rationale: PR 41656 is a concrete but unmerged implementation attempt for the same AUMID-qualified history identity. It is not a released fix, so this assessment records active coverage rather than claiming resolution.

issue_context.summary: Edge PWAs share a browser executable but need distinct FancyZones placement identities; the scenario is already under active canonical tracking.
known_information: The report concerns approximately a dozen Edge PWAs on PowerToys 0.100.2.
Different PWAs can open in the zone most recently used by another PWA.
Issue 652 remains open for this behavior and Issue 34713 was consolidated there.
PR 41656 provides an unmerged AppUserModelID-qualified history-key implementation.
inferences: The shared process identity is likely the mechanism, but it was not independently reproduced with the reporter's PWAs.
The AUMID approach is already being implemented, so another competing design would duplicate active work.
issue_context.analysis: The live report matches the canonical PWA placement tracker and its concrete implementation attempt. The public action accurately distinguishes active, unmerged coverage from a shipped fix.
initial_investigation: Read the full live issue and timeline.
Inspected AppZoneHistory.cpp and AppZoneHistory.h history-key use.
Reviewed upstream PR 41656 and the active fork-side adaptation referenced by its work.

actions.label: Close as duplicate of the FancyZones PWA tracker

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed report. This is the same FancyZones last-known-zone identity problem already tracked in #652. The current implementation attempt is #41656, which qualifies FancyZones' zone-history identity with the window's AppUserModelID so Edge PWAs and browser profiles can be distinguished. That PR is still open and under review, so the change is not yet available in a PowerToys release. Closing this issue as a duplicate of #652; please keep further tracking and validation on that issue.
